name: Plant milks, non-soy non-rice
anchor: Per-form sovereign beverage cells in the as-consumed liquid basis (EU 2023/915 juice and rice-drink cells, Codex CXS 193 fruit juices, EU 2024/1987 beverage nickel, EU canned-beverage tin, Hong Kong Cap 132V's named carbonated, tea, coffee and wine beverage entries, and the US and Hong Kong packaged-drinking-water quality standards), with dry leaf, bean and powder commodities anchored separately in their own as-sold basis and never converted between the two
native_basis_label: ready-to-drink liquid, as consumed (wet weight, single strength); a concentrate or a powder-to-liquid product is assessed as reconstituted to single strength per the manufacturer's own directions, which is the basis EU 2023/915 and Codex CXS 193 write into their juice cells and Hong Kong Cap 132V Note 11 writes into its beverage entries
scope_note: Ready-to-drink plant-based milk alternatives made from a base other than soy or rice: almond, oat, cashew, coconut, hemp, pea, macadamia, walnut, flax and blends of those. Includes shelf-stable and refrigerated formats and canned coconut milk sold as a beverage. Soy-based drinks route to the soy row (a distinct nickel and aluminium accumulation profile); any rice content routes the product to the rice-based row and its dedicated EU inorganic-arsenic cell. A plant-based infant formula routes to Category 1 by the taxonomy boundary rule; a plant-based drink carrying a Supplement Facts panel routes to Category 16; culinary canned coconut milk sold as an ingredient rather than a beverage routes to the pantry categories.
basis_guard: as[ _]consumed|wet weight|reconstituted|ready.to.drink|product as placed on market|\bjuice\b|single-strength|bottled water|portion ordinarily consumed
basis_guard_note: This row publishes a ready-to-drink liquid ceiling, so every named anchor must itself be written in a wet as-consumed (or as-placed-on-market liquid, or packaged-drinking-water) basis. The guard refuses any dry-commodity as-sold cell, any feed-basis cell, any food-contact migration limit and any article-content limit, because applying a dry leaf, bean or powder maximum level to a brewed or reconstituted liquid would be exactly the basis conflation Method v2.0 forbids. No brewing, dilution or reconstitution factor is invented in either direction.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only): the strictest applicable sovereign maximum level for this exact beverage form and analyte in the row's declared native basis, with disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated, a substantiated not-material determination where a species is bounded or is a method artifact, and a control where no defensible sovereign number and no supportable near-neighbour exist. Never occurrence-derived. Ready-to-drink and dry-commodity bases are never mixed and no brewing, dilution or reconstitution factor is invented.

Pb.basis: as consumed, ready-to-drink liquid (read across from the sovereign dairy-milk cell)
Pb.label: No credible sovereign has written a lead maximum level for a plant-based drink. The nearest applicable sovereign value is the Hong Kong Cap 132V lead cell for Milk (20 ug/kg, as consumed), the dairy beverage this product form substitutes for and shares a serving format, consumption pattern and liquid as-consumed basis with. It is adopted by disclosed read-across.
Pb.substantiation: A almond, oat, cashew, coconut, hemp or pea drink is not milk, and this is stated rather than glossed: the read-across rests on form and use, not on composition. The candidate set was the sovereign cells reachable in the same as-consumed liquid basis: the Hong Kong milk cell (20 ug/kg), the EU and Codex fruit-juice cells (30 ug/kg, a juice this product is not), and the Hong Kong carbonated-beverage cell (200 ug/kg, a carbonation form this product does not take). The milk cell is both the nearest by form and use and the strictest of those three, so no convenience selection is available among them. The packaged-drinking-water quality standards are stricter still (US 21 CFR 165.110 lead at 5 ug/kg, Hong Kong packaged drinking water at 10 ug/kg) and were considered and rejected on applicability: they govern water sold as water, they are Category 8 instruments under the taxonomy boundary rule, and a plant-based drink is an opaque formulated beverage carrying several percent suspended and dissolved plant solids plus mineral fortificants, which is not the matrix those standards were written for. The row's nut, oat and seed bases are grown in soils whose lead burden varies by origin, which is why lead is a mandatory lot test and a Standards Ratchet surveillance analyte here rather than a formality. The dry-commodity lead cells for the source seed, grain or nut are written in an as-sold dry basis and are deliberately NOT applied to the liquid drink; converting between them would require an invented dilution factor, which Method v2.0 confines to the infant-formula 8:1 reconstitution and forbids elsewhere.

Cd.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a cadmium maximum level for a non-soy non-rice plant-based drink. EU 2023/915, Codex CXS 193, FSANZ Schedule 19, Health Canada and Hong Kong Cap 132V set no cadmium maximum level for a plant-based drink, and none of them sets a cadmium cell for dairy milk either, so the dairy-milk analog relied on for lead and total mercury in this row supplies nothing for cadmium. The sovereign cadmium cells for the dry source seeds, grains and nuts (for example soy beans at 200 ug/kg) are as-sold dry-commodity values and cannot be carried into a ready-to-drink liquid without an invented dilution factor. No near-neighbour read-across is supportable, so the fail-safe disposition is a control: cadmium testing is mandatory on every certified lot and no ceiling is invented from occurrence data.
Cd.reference_method: Cadmium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. A result above 10 ug/kg in a ready-to-drink form, or above 100 ug/kg in a dry form, escalates to an ingredient-origin and process-water investigation and is a Standards Ratchet surveillance input under Governance Policy section 12.

tAs.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-arsenic maximum level for a non-soy non-rice plant-based drink. Regulators write beverage arsenic limits on the inorganic species (EU 2023/915 section 3.4.4 fruit juices at 20 ug/kg and section 3.4.1.6 non-alcoholic rice-based drinks at 30 ug/kg; the US FDA apple-juice action level at 10 ug/kg) and write unspeciated arsenic limits only in the packaged-water and public-water-supply schedules, which are Category 8 instruments. The inorganic-arsenic cell in this row carries the health-relevant fraction. Total arsenic is therefore mandatory on every lot as the parent screen and no total-arsenic ceiling is invented.
tAs.reference_method: Total arsenic by ICP-MS on every certified lot. Inorganic-arsenic speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS) is reflexed whenever total arsenic exceeds 50 percent of this row's inorganic-arsenic ceiling, or 20 ug/kg where this row publishes no inorganic-arsenic number. Species never substitute for the total: the iAs result does not satisfy the tAs reporting requirement.

iAs.basis: wet weight, ready-to-drink liquid (read across from the EU fruit-juice inorganic-arsenic cell)
iAs.source_scope: fruit juices, concentrated fruit juices as reconstituted, and fruit nectars
iAs.label: No credible sovereign has written an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for a non-rice plant-based drink. The EU 2023/915 section 3.4.4 fruit-juice cell (20 ug/kg) is the strictest sovereign inorganic-arsenic value written for a general ready-to-drink beverage and is adopted by disclosed read-across in the identical liquid basis.
iAs.substantiation: The obvious alternative, the EU non-alcoholic rice-based drinks cell (30 ug/kg), is the nearer analog by product family but is written for the rice inorganic-arsenic hazard specifically, and this row excludes rice; adopting a rice-drink allowance for an oat, almond or coconut drink would import a hazard allowance the product does not earn, and it is looser. The fruit-juice cell is therefore adopted as both applicable and stricter. The US FDA apple-juice action level (10 ug/kg) is scoped to a single named fruit commodity and is not applicable. Any rice content routes the product to the rice-based row and its dedicated EU cell.

tHg.basis: as consumed, ready-to-drink liquid (read across from the sovereign dairy-milk cell)
tHg.label: No credible sovereign has written a total-mercury maximum level for a plant-based drink. The Hong Kong Cap 132V total-mercury cell for Milk (10 ug/kg, as consumed) is the nearest applicable sovereign value in the identical liquid as-consumed basis and is adopted by disclosed read-across, consistent with the lead cell in this row.
tHg.substantiation: Mercury has no identified enrichment pathway in a nut, oat or seed drink, but Method v2.0 prefers a disclosed read-across from the nearest applicable sovereign value over a bare control where one exists, and the dairy-milk cell is the same analog already relied on for lead in this row, so the two cells are anchored consistently rather than opportunistically. The US 21 CFR 165.110 bottled-water total-mercury value (2 ug/kg) was considered and rejected: it is a packaged-water quality standard for water sold as water (Category 8), and a plant-based drink is a formulated beverage with substantial dissolved and suspended solids, not water. Methylmercury remains bounded by this total.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury has no formation pathway in a plant-based drink: there is no marine bioaccumulation step in the supply chain and no anaerobic, sulfate-reducing methylation environment in the product or its process. Methylmercury is a component of total mercury (MeHg <= tHg) and is governed by and bounded by the total-mercury cell; no separate methylmercury ceiling is published.
MeHg.reference_method: Bounded by the total-mercury cell (tHg). Methylmercury speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS or GC-ICP-MS) is reflexed only on an elevated total-mercury result; it is not a routine lot test for this form.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a methylmercury limit for any beverage, leaf, bean or beverage powder. Methylmercury maximum levels are scoped to fish, seafood and other marine matrices (EU 2023/915 section 3.3, US FDA CPG 540.600, Hong Kong Cap 132V fish entries). Methylmercury is a species of and bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg), which this row controls directly.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915 (and EU 2024/1987 for nickel, EU 2025/1891 for arsenic in seafood); Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (21 CFR 165.110 bottled-water quality standards, Juice HACCP guidance, Closer to Zero action levels); FSANZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19; Health Canada List of Contaminants and Other Adulterating Substances; UK retained maximum levels; Hong Kong Cap 132V (Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) Regulations) — none sets a methylmercury limit for this product form.

Ni.basis: product as placed on market, ready-to-drink liquid (read across from the EU beverage nickel cell)
Ni.label: No credible sovereign has written a nickel maximum level for a plant-based drink. EU 2024/1987's fruit and vegetable juices and nectars cell (250 ug/kg) is the only sovereign nickel value written for a ready-to-drink beverage and is adopted by disclosed read-across as the nearest applicable value in the identical liquid basis.
Ni.substantiation: Oat and tree-nut bases are moderate nickel accumulators, so this is a live cell rather than a formality: EU 2024/1987 assigns oats 5000 ug/kg and tree nuts 3500 ug/kg in the dry commodity. EU 2024/1987 does write nickel cells for the dry source commodities (cereals 800 ug/kg, oats 5000 ug/kg, tree nuts 3500 ug/kg, soy beans 6000 to 15000 ug/kg), and those cells are deliberately NOT applied here: they are as-sold dry-commodity values, and carrying one into a ready-to-drink liquid would require an invented dilution factor. The infant and young-child formula nickel cells (100 ug/kg liquid, 250 ug/kg powder, 400 ug/kg soy-isolate powder) are Category 1 instruments and are excluded from this category's anchor set by the taxonomy boundary rule, not borrowed. Nickel is a Tier-2 analyte and this cell is a surveillance priority for the Standards Ratchet.

Sn.basis: product as placed on market, ready-to-drink liquid (inorganic tin)
Sn.label: EU 2023/915 Annex I section 3.5.2 sets inorganic tin in canned beverages, including canned fruit and vegetable juices, at 100 mg/kg = 100000 ug/kg; Hong Kong Cap 132V sets canned beverages at 150000 ug/kg. The EU value is the strictest applicable and binds. This is a direct sovereign maximum level on the beverage-in-a-can form, not a read-across.
Sn.substantiation: Tin in a beverage is a tinplate and can-lining migration pathway, so the government instruments are written on the canned form and the canned form is where the hazard sits. The EU cell (100000 ug/kg) directly governs every canned or tinplate-packaged product in this row and is adopted as the row ceiling for all packaging formats; a carton, PET, glass or pouch format has no tin source and complies trivially, so no separate non-canned cell is published. The looser Hong Kong canned-beverage cell (150000) and the canned-foods cells for solid foods (EU 200000; Codex, FSANZ and Hong Kong 250000) are disclosed and deliberately not adopted: EU writes a stricter cell specifically for beverages and HMTc preserves that product-form split. Tin is a Tier-2 analyte; an elevated result in a non-canned format is a packaging-integrity signal.

Al.rationale: No credible sovereign sets an aluminium maximum level for a non-soy non-rice plant-based drink. The only sovereign aluminium values in a dietary basis are the packaged-drinking-water quality standards (US 21 CFR 165.110 secondary allowable level 200 ug/kg, EU 2020/2184, Health Canada 2900 ug/kg), which govern water sold as water and are Category 8 instruments, and the FSANZ infant-formula aluminium limits, which are Category 1 and are excluded from this category's anchor set by the taxonomy boundary rule. In this form aluminium is a packaging and processing signal (aluminium cans and can linings, closures, filter aids, additive carry-over) rather than a raw-material contaminant. Plant-based drinks additionally carry mineral-fortification premixes and stabiliser systems, so an aluminium result is investigated against the fortificant and stabiliser specifications as well as the packaging.
Al.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. A result that departs materially from the applicant's own documented process baseline escalates to a packaging, can-lining and processing-aid investigation. This is a process-control tripwire, not a numeric standard: no ceiling is published because no credible sovereign maximum exists for this cell.

Cr.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-chromium maximum level for a non-soy non-rice plant-based drink. The only sovereign chromium values reachable from this basis family are the packaged-drinking-water quality standards (US 21 CFR 165.110 at 100 ug/kg, Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged drinking water at 50 ug/kg), which govern water sold as water and are Category 8 instruments, and the public-water-system maximum contaminant levels (US EPA, Health Canada), which are water-utility instruments and not food law at all. Total chromium in this form is dominated by benign Cr(III) and is reported as a stainless-steel equipment and process-water leaching screen, not as a health limit; the health-relevant species is addressed in the Cr-VI cell.
Cr.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. An elevated result triggers the Cr(VI) speciation reflex and an equipment, process-water and ingredient investigation.

Cr-VI.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a hexavalent-chromium limit for any food or beverage, and the in-matrix reduction argument that supports a not-material determination in an acidic beverage is not available here: a plant-based drink is near-neutral (typically pH 6.5 to 7.5) and low in the organic acids and ascorbate that drive Cr(VI) reduction in an acidic beverage, so the reduction cannot be assumed. Because Cr(VI) cannot be assumed to be reduced to Cr(III) in this matrix, the fail-safe disposition is a control rather than a not-material determination, and no ceiling is invented.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every certified lot. Cr(VI)-specific speciation (IC-ICP-MS, EN 15192 adapted) is reflexed whenever total chromium exceeds 100 ug/kg in this form, or 50 percent of the total-chromium screen value where this row publishes one. A confirmed Cr(VI) detection escalates to a process-water, equipment and ingredient investigation and blocks certification pending resolution.
